newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeris eye four more oil deals with foreign firms.
newsitem.headline: Azeris eye four more oil deals with foreign firms.

text.p: Azerbaijan's state-owned oil company SOCAR plans to sign four major contracts with foreign firms to develop offshore Caspian reserves by the end of the year, the company's president said on Wednesday.

Natik Aliyev said the deals planned are with Exxon, Mobil and Chevron of the United States, and a consortium of Japanese firms including ITOCHU, Indonesia Petroleum Ltd (INPEX), state-owned Japan National Oil Corp (JNOC) and Japan Petroleum Exploration Co Ltd (JAPEX).

"This year we will sign a contract with Exxon (on three fields). We are close to signing with Chevron (and) Mobil," he said at the Fourth Annual International Caspian Oil & Gas Exhibition and Conference in Baku.
Aliyev said the Exxon-SOCAR deal involves three deep water fields, designated D-3, D-9, and D-38 located between 50 and 100 km (30 and 60 miles) offshore in the South Caspian.
SOCAR geologists have given estimates of over 100 million tonnes of recoverable oil reserves at the fields.
Exxon government affairs manager James Riley said it was too early to say how much the deal would be worth or what SOCAR and Exxon's shares in the project would be.
"We hope to have things finalised within six months or so," he told Reuters.
Aliyev also said SOCAR would sign with Chevron on developing the Zeinalabdin-Tagiyev field, about 80 kilometers offshore.
SOCAR has given estimates of at least 115 million tonnes of recoverable reserves of oil and 420 billion cubic metres (bcm) of natural gas at the site.
Aliyev said a SOCAR-Mobil project involved the Oguz and D-30 sites in the South Caspian. SOCAR pegs estimated crude reserves there at 40 million tonnes of oil or more, and 20 bcm of gas.
Japan's Itochu, JNOC, JAPEX and INPEX are involved in the fourth proposed project to develop the Yanan Tava, Ateshgakh-3 and Mugan Deniz sites, which cover 500 square km in the southwest Caspian.
No details were immediately available on possible reserves at the fields or what the project may be worth, but Aliyev said a deal with the four firms would be signed by the end of 1997.
Azerbaijan has signed five deals with foreign firms worth over $18 billion in total investment to develop its huge Caspian reserves.
The largest contract is the Azerbaijan International Operating Company (AIOC) worth $8 billion. It is a 13-member consortium led by British Petroleum and Statoil (Den norse stats oljeselskap).
It was hailed the "contract of the century" when it was signed in 1994.
